summary: Rivian has strategic capital support from Volkswagen and has started R2 production, and independent reports point to strong R2 demand. Against that are repeated 2025 guidance cuts, R1 demand that has flattened near a ~$90k price point, continuing layoffs, and cash intensity. The investment case depends on R2 execution and margins, which the sources do not yet show clearly.

facts.text: Rivian delivered 13,201 vehicles in Q3 2025 and narrowed full-year 2025 guidance to 41,500–43,500. That was its second cut of the year, down from up to 51,000 at the start of 2025, and below its 2023 and 2024 deliveries.
Rivian's own Q3 2025 results report 78% year-over-year consolidated revenue growth and $24 million of consolidated gross profit. These figures are self-reported.
Volkswagen bought 62.9 million new shares at $15.90 (about $1B) on April 30, 2026. That made VW the largest shareholder at 15.9%; Amazon's stake was diluted to about 11.8%.

VW has deployed about $3.3B of its up to $5.8B commitment. Further tranches are milestone-contingent and tied to the RV Tech joint venture, whose first VW models running Rivian software are expected in 2027.
Rivian posted $1.38B of revenue in Q1 2026 and began R2 production at Normal, Illinois.
A $250M securities class action settlement covering IPO-era disclosures received final court approval on May 29, 2026. This removes a legal overhang.
A third-party report says Rivian beat quarterly delivery estimates in Q3 2026 on strong R2 demand. Stifel maintained a Buy rating and a $22 target, citing R2 orders.

Competitors in the electric pickup and SUV segment include the Tesla Cybertruck, Chevy Silverado EV, Slate Truck, and VW's Scout Terra and Traveler. Scout's entry pricing is expected under $60,000, with production targeted for 2027.

risks.text: R1 demand appears to have hit a ceiling, according to InsideEVs and comments from the CEO. That makes the R2 launch make-or-break for the company.
Policy headwinds include the expiration of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit and tariffs, both cited for guidance cuts and analyst target reductions.
Rivian remains cash-intensive. VW tranches extend its runway but dilute existing shareholders through private placements.
Repeated workforce reductions point to cost pressure: at least five cuts since June 2025, including more than 600 jobs in October 2025 and a cut in Title & Registration staff in October 2026.
Scout Motors is VW-backed and targets the adjacent rugged EV truck and SUV segment. It could compete with Rivian even as VW is Rivian's partner.
Some owners report quality issues such as cabin noise and rattles. This evidence is anecdotal and comes from Reddit forums.

open_questions: What are R2 unit economics and gross margin at scale, and when does Rivian expect sustained positive gross profit?
What are current cash, burn rate, and runway, and which remaining VW milestones (about $2.5B) are at risk?
How large and how durable is the R2 order backlog, beyond analyst and press reports?
How are conflicts handled between VW's Scout brand and Rivian in overlapping segments?
What is the status and volume of the Amazon delivery van relationship now that Amazon's stake is diluted?
